title: Open-quantum-system theory of non-Markovian electron-phonon dynamics
authors: Gabriele Riva, Jacopo Simoni, Yuan Ping
abstract: We present a non-Markovian open quantum dynamics formalism for the study of nonequilibrium electron-phonon interactions, based on a closed set of four coupled equations of motion for the electronic one-body reduced density matrix, the phonon density matrix, the coherent phonon, and the electron-phonon correlations. Memory effects in the electronic dynamics emerge naturally from the coupling between the electronic density matrix and the electron-phonon correlation equations, beyond the Markovian approximation. The formalism treats coherent-phonon dynamics and dissipative broadening on an equal footing, making it particularly suited to polaron formation and the finite lifetimes of driven electronic excitations. In appropriate limits it recovers the Fan-Migdal, polarization in random-phase-approximation, and Ehrenfest self-energies of nonequilibrium Green's function theory, as well as the Lindblad and Boltzmann equations, while avoiding the storage of two-time correlators. To drive the system out of equilibrium, we study its interaction with an external time-dependent field. As an illustrative application, we benchmark our theory against the exact solution of the Holstein dimer under a strong external perturbation, where the non-Markovian dynamics correctly captures dissipative spectral broadening and energy conservation.
summary: The paper introduces an advanced, non-Markovian open quantum system theory to study electron-phonon interactions beyond simple approximations. By deriving a closed set of four coupled equations of motion, the authors successfully model complex memory effects and energy exchange in systems like polarons. This framework is validated by reproducing known theoretical limits and matching benchmark results from exact solutions.
main_problem: Developing a fully quantum, non-perturbative treatment of nonequilibrium electron–phonon coupling that captures quantum coherence, memory effects, and dissipative dynamics.
main_result: The proposed formalism successfully captures spectral broadening and energy conservation in comparison to simpler approximations, correctly modeling complex many-body correlations inherent in the system.
method: It employs an open quantum system theory approach using a closed set of four coupled equations of motion for reduced density matrices, avoiding the storage of two-time correlators.
model_or_system: The study models electron-phonon coupled systems, governed by a Hamiltonian including electronic, phonon, and coupling terms. It is benchmarked against the exact solution of the Holstein dimer under external driving fields.
key_observables: Spectral functions (via Fourier transform of polarization P(t)), total energy conservation, and various self-energies (Fan-Migdal, RPA Polarization, Ehrenfest).
important_parameters: Dimensionless coupling constants $\gamma = \omega_{	ext{ph}}/t_{	ext{hop}}$ and $\lambda = 2g^2/(t_{	ext{hop}}\omega_{	ext{ph}})$; the comparison between coherent vs. non-Markovian dynamics.
main_assumptions: The formalism involves truncating the hierarchy of equations at second order in the electron-phonon matrix element, while treating coherent and dissipative dynamics on an equal footing.
figures_summary: Figure 1 diagrammatically shows how various self-energies arise from coupling different equations. Subsequent figures compare spectra obtained from exact solutions against those derived from the full non-Markovian set versus a simplified coherent approximation.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the Hamiltonian and the need for a non-Markovian formalism, derives the closed set of four coupled equations of motion (EOMs), discusses how these EOMs recover known limits (Lindblad, Boltzmann, etc.), and finally applies the theory to benchmark against exact solutions using time evolution simulations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, systematic theoretical framework for open quantum systems in condensed matter that naturally incorporates memory effects and treats coherence alongside dissipation, which is crucial for understanding polaron physics and ultrafast dynamics.

FIG. 2. Dynamics of the occupation of the first site for dif- ferent level of theories. Exact dynamics (solid red curve), coherent phonons dynamics (dotted blue curve), and non- Markovian dynamics (dot-dashed green curve). The dynamics is obtained with λ = 0.5 and γ = 0.5

FIG. 3. Spectra as a function of γ for small e-ph interaction λ = 0.05. (a) Exact result. (b) Coupled Eqs. (14a) and (14e). (c) Solution of the full set of non-Markovian equations (14a)-(14e). We observe single phonon absorption and emission (S) with slope ±γ starting from E = 4, and two-phonon absorption and emission (D) with slope ±2γ starting from E = 2, and a single phonon absorption starting (S) and a three-phonon absorption (T) from E = 0. This last contribution is visible only for γ >∼1.

FIG. 4. Spectra as a function of the dimensionless coupling constant λ. (a) Exact result. (b) Coupled Eqs. (14a) and (14e). (c) Solution of the full set of non-Markovian equations (14a)-(14e). The Non-Markovian result shows a broadening of the peaks similarly to the exact result, the coherent phonon-electron dynamics do not capture this feature.

FIG. 5. Comparison between different energy contributions in Eq. (22). Black curve, total energy. Red, blue and green line, energy contributions of the electron, phonon and electron-phonon correlation, respectively. Left panel, exact result. Right panel, non-Markovian dynamics. Insets, zoom on the variation of the total energy due to the external pump. This plot is obtained for λ = 0.5 and γ = 0.5.
